key_entities: plan-review criteria E4 T2 T3 T5b
propositions: A primary comment dedup guard (_record_comment_id) was inert in production because the comment_ids map in .bridge_state/bindings.json was never populated, surviving the entire feature's 6-day lifecycle from deploy to fix

The guard failed silently without logging or metrics, and a secondary fallback (body-equality skip) absorbed enough traffic to mask the defect as partial success rather than total primary-path failure

Existing unit tests cover both shores of the dedup seam (apply-side recording and differ-side skipping) but do not cross the seam, seeding the invariant each layer expects the other to establish rather than verifying the connection end-to-end

All existing plan-review and code-review criteria had scope boundaries drawn just short of the escape: E4 abstains on external system claims, T3 stops at endpoint existence rather than response schema, T5b addresses plans not code guards, and fail-open detection was added post-escape

An operation-linked runtime invariant (bridge_alerts check for successful comment posts paired with zero comment_ids growth) is the only layer uncovered after review-time rubrics, representing the cheapest candidate remedy
